I say that the base BC is also equal to the base EF, the triangle ABC will be equal to the triangle DEF, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend, thatis, the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle ACB to the angle DFE. For, if the triangle ABC be applied to the triangle DEF, and if the point A be placed on the point D and the straight line AB on DE, then the point B will also coincide with E, because AB is equal to DE. Again, AB coinciding with DE, the straight line AC will also coincide with DF, because the angle BAC is equal to the angle EDF; hence the point C will also coincide with the point F, because AC is again equal to DF. But B also coincided with E; hence the base BC will coincide with the base EF. **Statement:** If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

**Step 1.** Let ABC and DEF be two triangles having the two sides AB, AC equal to the two sides DE, DF respectively, namely AB equal to DE and AC equal to DF, and having the angle BAC equal to the angle EDF. We must show that the base BC is equal to the base EF, that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF, and that the remaining angles are equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend: the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle ACB to the angle DFE.

**Step 2.** Apply the triangle ABC to the triangle DEF so that the point A is placed on the point D and the straight line AB is placed along the straight line DE. Since AB is equal to DE, the point B will coincide with the point E, for the two equal straight lines AB and DE laid out from the same point D in the same direction reach the same point.

**Step 3.** Since AB now lies along DE, and the angle BAC is equal to the angle EDF, the straight line AC will fall along the straight line DF; for the inclination of AC to AB is the same as the inclination of DF to DE, so that AC, laid off from D on the same side of DE as DF, takes the same direction as DF.

**Step 4.** Since AC is equal to DF, the point C will coincide with the point F, for the two equal straight lines AC and DF laid out from the same point D along the same straight line reach the same point.

**Step 5.** Now B coincides with E and C coincides with F. The base BC is the straight line joining B to C, and the base EF is the straight line joining E to F; by P1 the straight line joining two given points is a determinate straight line, so that there is only one straight line from E to F. If BC did not coincide with EF while B lay on E and C on F, two distinct straight lines would join the same two points E and F and would enclose a space, which is impossible. Therefore the base BC coincides with the base EF.

**Step 6.** Since the base BC coincides with the base EF, the base BC is equal to the base EF (CN4).

**Step 7.** Since the point A coincides with D, B with E, and C with F, and the sides AB, AC, BC coincide with the sides DE, DF, EF respectively, the whole triangle ABC coincides with the whole triangle DEF; therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF (CN4).

**Step 8.** Likewise, the side BA coincides with ED and the side BC with EF, so the angle ABC, contained by BA and BC, coincides with the angle DEF, contained by ED and EF; therefore the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF (CN4). And the side CA coincides with FD and the side CB with FE, so the angle ACB coincides with the angle DFE; therefore the angle ACB is equal to the angle DFE (CN4).

**Step 9.** Thus the base BC is equal to the base EF, the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF, and the remaining angles are equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely the angle ABC (subtended by AC) to the angle DEF (subtended by DF), and the angle ACB (subtended by AB) to the angle DFE (subtended by DE). This is what was to be proved.
